conviction_note: Nothing sourced decides this print. The bar (about $800M revenue, $0.34 EPS) already carries a CELSIUS-brand decline of about 12% year on year, which is what management said in August that Q3 would look like. Alani Nu's channel data (+47% in c-stores, about +50% in IRI scans) and an above-consensus B. Riley model ($817.6M) tilt the reported quarter slightly toward a beat. Against that, the stock is up 11.8% in 5 days and 16% in 20, and this name has sold a beat by 24.8% before (Q3 2025, on forward 'noise'). So p_up is 52 and abs_move is 13, above the 10.9% implied move because the name's own median reaction is 17.3%. Findings sum to +0.6; the scaled number is +0.52. They agree in sign, and both are small.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus revenue $800.6M and EPS $0.34 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-5-celsius-holdings-inc-stock/, read 2026-11-04). B. Riley also cites $800.6M and Jefferies $795M (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/briley-reiterates-buy-on-celsius-stock-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4990506). Benzinga shows $802.6M and $0.35. Earnings Whispers alone shows $854M and $0.37, an outlier. Two or more sources agree within 1%, so the bar is treated as sourced. The company gives no numeric guidance. Its only Q3 guide is qualitative, from the 2026-08-06 call: the CELSIUS brand looks 'a lot like Q2', gross margin stays in the high 40s, and gradual improvement starts in Q4.
positioning_check: Short interest was 30.11M shares with 5.5 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/celh, snapshot 2026-11-04). It was 30.96M shares and 4.5 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement. Benzinga put it at 13.8% of float in August 2026 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CELH/sentiment). That is moderately crowded, so the short can squeeze on a beat. The baseline 25-delta skew is -2.15 vol points, meaning calls are bid ('upside paid'), and the put/call open-interest ratio is 0.42. The 5-day run-up is +11.76%, the 20-day +16.16%, and the stock sits 47.8% below its 52-week high. The option market and the tape both lean long into the print.

findings.finding: The bar sits inside management's own Q3 framing. Consensus revenue of about $800M (+10% on Q3 2025's $725.1M) matches what follows from three numbers: CELSIUS brand Q2 2026 net sales of $387.0M (-11.7%), management's statement that Q3 brand sales will look 'a lot like Q2', and Jefferies' projection of CELSIUS brand sales down 12%. Q3 2025 brand sales were about $382.6M, so -12% gives about $337M. Add Rockstar at about $66M (Q2 run-rate) and the consensus needs Alani Nu at about $392M, +18% on Q3 2025's $332.0M. Alani tracked scans are running about +50%. B. Riley models $817.6M, about 2% above consensus, even after assuming about $35M of further inventory rebalancing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed by about 6% ($818M vs $870M) and the stock fell 18.46%. Q3 2025 beat on revenue ($725.1M vs $715.7M) and EPS (42c vs 28c), yet the stock fell 24.8% on Q4 'noise' commentary. Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 beats were bought (+6.9%, +4.5%). The reported-quarter line pays only when the forward commentary does not override it.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has already been cut (the revenue estimate fell 7.6% over three months per Chartmill, and targets were cut at JPM, UBS, TD Cowen and Jefferies). The gap between Alani's roughly 50% scan growth and the roughly 18% the bar needs is the part not in the consensus. Had the market priced a clear Alani-led beat, consensus would have moved back up toward the B. Riley number; it has not. Partly priced: the 5-day run-up of +11.8% suggests some of the street is already leaning toward a beat.
findings.independence: Brand decline rate and Q3 framing: the 8-K Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001341766/000134176626000047/ex9912q2026.htm) and the call summary (https://www.chartmill.com/news/external/114221/celh-q2-earnings-call-flags-core-brand-reset-before-2027). Q3 2025 base: the 8-K Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1341766/000134176625000138/ex9913q2025.htm). The arithmetic is mine. The Jefferies figure and the B. Riley model come from the same Investing.com article.

findings.finding: The Goldman Sachs Q3 2026 c-store retailer survey shows the CELSIUS brand -1% year on year against an energy category +11% (+10% in Q2) and Alani Nu +47%. That is a stable CELSIUS brand, close to Q2's -2% tracked retail, not a further deterioration, plus strong Alani sell-through. Separately, IRI scans quoted around the 2026-09-08 Barclays conference showed CELSIUS -5% to -10% and Alani about +50%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 tracked retail was -2% but net sales were -11.7%, and the stock fell 18.5%. Scan-to-shipment gaps, not scans themselves, have driven the misses, so a sell-through proxy transmits only partly.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a channel survey published 2026-10-23 that wire previews do not quote, and it covers one channel. If it were fully priced, CELSIUS-brand estimates would not still sit at about -12%. The survey fits that number, since shipments trail sell-through while distributor inventory is rebalanced. So this is mostly confirmation that Alani is strong; it is not evidence of a brand beat.
findings.independence: Proxy, not company data. The IRI scan ranges are reported in the B. Riley/Investing.com note (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/briley-reiterates-buy-on-celsius-stock-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4990506) and in the TIKR Barclays recap (https://www.tikr.com/es/blog/celsius-stock-slid-nearly-7-after-barclays-and-the-real-payoff-it-described-waits-until-2027). KDP's Q3 also says the energy category kept growing: Ghost passed $1B retail and KDP energy share passed 10%.

findings.finding: The forward line is the risk, and management has already deferred the payoff. On the Q2 call it said the CELSIUS brand improves only gradually from Q4 and returns to growth in 2027, and that the Q4 Alani Nu comparison is distorted by the prior-year inventory build for the PepsiCo transition. At Barclays (2026-09-08) the CFO said the real dollars from revenue management are 'a game for '27 and '28', not a rescue for H2 2026. There is room for Q4 commentary that resets Alani Q4 below the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 beat on revenue and EPS but fell 24.8% when the CFO warned of Q4 'noise' from the Alani/Pepsi rollout. Forward commentary has decided at least two of the last seven reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The deferral itself is public, which is why the stock fell after Barclays and targets were cut. What is not priced is the size of the Q4 Alani comparison headwind, which the company has never quantified. A run-up of +11.8% in five days into the print suggests some holders are positioned for an H2 inflection that management has said is a 2027 event.
findings.independence: Same deferral reported from the Barclays session: https://www.tikr.com/es/blog/celsius-stock-slid-nearly-7-after-barclays-and-the-real-payoff-it-described-waits-until-2027. Q4 2025 Alani inventory build: https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/celsius-cfo-warns-of-q4-noise-amid-alani-nu-pepsi-rollout-but-retail-goes-contrarian/cL2twoqRERY (Nov 2025).

findings.finding: Expectations are rising into the print. The stock is +11.76% in 5 days and +16.16% in 20 (31.27 against the 23.77 close after Q2), calls are bid (25-delta skew -2.15), and put/call open interest is 0.42. No company or analyst catalyst explains the last week. I found no upgrades between 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-03, and the last rating action was JPM cutting its target to $48 on 10-26. Against that, about 30.1M shares are short (5.5 days to cover), which supplies squeeze fuel on a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Before Q2 2026 the stock had bottomed near $24 and fell another 18.5% on the miss. After an activist-driven rally in August, it fell about 7% after Barclays when the payoff was pushed to 2027.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The question is whether the run-up raised the bar for the reaction above the consensus number. A crowded short makes a negative less likely to follow through, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline tape and options block (run_up_5d_pct 11.76, skew -2.15). Rating actions: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/celh/ and https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CELH/.

findings.finding: Insiders bought in the open market mid-quarter, after the Q2 miss: CEO John Fieldly 18,000 shares at about $27.44, director Damon DeSantis about $1.0M at an average of $27.78 in September 2026, and director Hal Kravitz about $1.0M across three filings. About $2.7M across four insiders, with EDGAR Form 4s dated 2026-08-11, 09-10, 09-15 and 09-16. These were bought while Q3 was in progress and visible to them.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior comparable insider-buying cluster in the baseline window. A buying cluster says the insiders saw nothing that worried them mid-quarter. It does not size the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since September, and the stock has since risen from about $27.5 to $31.3, so part of it is priced. If it were fully priced as a signal of a strong quarter, consensus would have stopped falling; it was still being cut in October (JPM, TD Cowen, UBS).
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions show Form 4s on 2026-08-11, 2026-09-10, 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001341766.json). TIKR reports four insiders bought about $1.94M between Aug 6 and Sep 14 (https://www.tikr.com/es/blog/celsius-stock-while-an-activist-demanded-a-new-ceo-its-actual-ceo-was-buying-and-so-were-three-other-insiders).

findings.finding: The distributor's Q3 (12 weeks to 2026-09-05) was weak. PepsiCo Beverages North America had organic revenue 0% and organic volume -3%, and PepsiCo cut FY26 core EPS growth to +2.5-3.5% from 5-7%. Management reportedly said it is competing well in energy and hydration. Celsius sells almost all its US volume through Pepsi, so Pepsi destocking or tighter inventory management is the swing factor for shipments against scans.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pepsi inventory management drove the 2024 destock (a $100-120M Q3 2024 order cut) and the Q2 2026 rebalancing gap. Both were sold hard.
findings.why_not_priced: Pepsi's weakness was in soft drinks, and the filing says nothing about energy inventory. The transmission to Celsius is an inference, so this is sized small. It has been public for four weeks.
findings.independence: AP coverage of the same release: https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/ap-top-news/2026/10/08/pepsico-sees-strong-overseas-demand-but-a-lackluster-north-american-performance-in-the-third-quarter. The energy remark comes from an AI podcast summary (https://betafinch.com/episodes/PEP_2026_Q3_en). It is a proxy.

findings.finding: Can costs peaked inside Q3 cost of goods. The US Midwest aluminum premium hit a record of about $1.19/lb in June 2026 and eased only to about $1.09-1.10 by mid-September. Can pricing passes through with a lag of two to three months, so Q3 gross margin carries the peak. Management guided gross margin to the high 40s (Q2: 48.1%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 gross margin was 48.1% (-340bp year on year) and the EBITDA miss contributed to the -18.5% move.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. It sits inside the company's high-40s guide, and consensus EPS of $0.34 is below Q2's $0.36. Only an outcome below 47% would be new.
findings.independence: Mysteel on the pass-through lag: https://www.mysteel.net/news/5103982-us-aluminum-midwest-premiums-hit-record-high-what-drives-the-surge-and-who-bears-the-cost. It is a proxy.

findings.finding: Governance pressure is live. Rockstar founder Russ Savage disclosed a stake of about 4.7% (about 12M shares) on 2026-08-07 and demanded the CEO's removal. The President and COO departed by 8-K on 2026-08-10, and a new chief commercial officer was named. The Q3 call is the first earnings call since then, and any announcement of leadership or strategy changes on it would land in the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stake disclosure moved the stock +12-13% in one session (2026-08-07).
findings.why_not_priced: The stake itself is priced. No 13D, proxy filing or settlement has appeared on EDGAR since (the last filings are Form 4s and a 13G/A on 08-14), so any call-day governance news would be new. Its probability is unknown, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: COO departure 8-K, 2026-08-10 (items 5.02 and 7.01), in EDGAR submissions: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001341766.json. TIKR: https://www.tikr.com/blog/rockstars-founder-wants-celsiuss-ceo-fired-days-later-the-coo-was-gone.

findings.finding: Buyback capacity is large against the market cap. Cash was $631.2M on 2026-06-30. The company used $124.5M of a $300M authorization in H1, $100.4M of it in Q2, which leaves about $175M. Shares outstanding fell to 253.3M from 256.9M. The term loan was refinanced on 2026-07-15 at a lower rate ($694.75M). A Q3 repurchase or a larger authorization is plausible with the stock near its lows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $100M Q2 buyback did not prevent the 18.5% fall, so this line has not moved the stock on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public. Only a new or enlarged authorization would be news. The refinancing reduces interest cost, and the money funds no visible ramp; it is a cheaper loan, not a growth bet.

findings.finding: Several law firms issued securities class-action notices against Celsius on 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03, with a lead-plaintiff deadline of 2026-11-03. I could not source the class period or the allegations, so this cannot be tied to a disclosure the call might have to address.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A 2024 suit over inventory oversold to PepsiCo did not register as a print-day driver in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Boilerplate law-firm notices; this is mostly noise. It is filed so the panel can see it.
findings.independence: Massive.com also lists the 2026-11-03 notices (https://massive.com/quote/celh). The same notices, not independent.

outside_window.finding: Management puts the real inflection in H1 2027: CELSIUS innovation returns, the SKU-cut drag laps, and the 2027 revenue-management program is called the biggest single opportunity. Alani Nu launches internationally in 2027.
Monster Beverage's Q3 2026 print, a read-across for the category, is not yet out and normally lands after this window.

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees with the option market's mild upside lean (skew -2.15, calls bid), but the +11.8% 5-day run-up has already spent part of a modest beat. That is why p_up is held at 52 rather than the high 50s the Alani channel data alone would support.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the consensus-arithmetic finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5, because the bar matches management's own 'Q3 like Q2' framing; print_vs_bar cut from +1.5 to +1.0
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): this name sold a Q3 2025 beat by 24.8% on forward commentary; insider buying cut from +0.7 to +0.5 and p_up moved from 53 to 52
Lesson 7 (crowded short against a negative): positioning negative cut from -0.5 to -0.3 given 30M shares short and 5.5 days to cover
Lesson 5 (proxy): PepsiCo distributor transmission cut from -0.3 to -0.2; aluminum cut from -0.3 to -0.1 because it sits inside the high-40s gross-margin guide
Lesson 9 (segment net): the Alani channel strength is sized net of the CELSIUS brand's roughly -12% and the $35M rebalancing; c-store finding trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4
Buyback cut from +0.3 to +0.2 (public authorization); class action from -0.2 to -0.1 (unsourced class period)
